data.gender_notes: Fasiya is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'fasaha', meaning 'to heal'. In Islamic tradition, Fasiya is a name given to a healer or a caregiver. The name signifies the nurturing and healing power of a mother or a caregiver. The name Fasiya carries the meaning “Healer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fasiya usually hope their child will grow to embody healer and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Fasiya belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Healer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fasiya total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.
